newsitem.title: USA: Wash D.C. sets phone interconnection terms.
newsitem.headline: Wash D.C. sets phone interconnection terms.

text.p: AT&T Corp said Tuesday the District of Columbia's Public Service Commission issued an order setting terms and conditions for allowing new entrants into the local phone business to hook up to Bell Atlantic Corp's local network.

The commission approved giving resellers such as AT&T who plan to provide their own directory assistance and operator services an interim 24.7 percent wholesale discount on Bell Atlantic's retail rates for local phone service until regulators complete proceedings for a permanent rate.
In addition, resellers will receive a 6.7 percent reduction for gross receipts tax.
The order applies to all new local phone providers who purchase Bell Atlantic's local service and resell it to District consumers and businesses.

"If the commission continues on this course of action to encourage fair competition, and Bell Atlantic cooperates as required and doesn't put up any more roadblocks, AT&T expects to be able to offer local service to all residents and businesses in the District of Columbia during 1997," said AT&T Vice President John Langhauser.
